setupNotes: Standing, hands behind head, elbows wide. Perform bodyweight squat. Hands behind head forces upright torso and challenges mobility.

name: Pistol Squat (Single-Leg) — Left Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the left leg, right leg extended forward off the floor. Squat down on the left leg to full depth — hip below knee — keeping the right leg lifted, then drive back to standing. Use a doorframe or TRX for assistance if needed. Advanced left-leg strength.

name: Pistol Squat (Single-Leg) — Right Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the right leg, left leg extended forward off the floor. Squat down on the right leg to full depth — hip below knee — keeping the left leg lifted, then drive back to standing. Use a doorframe or TRX for assistance if needed. Advanced right-leg strength.

name: Shrimp Squat — Left Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the left leg, hold the right foot behind you at the glute with the right hand. Squat down on the left leg until the right knee taps the floor, then drive back to standing. Advanced unilateral squat — heavy left quad and glute load.

name: Shrimp Squat — Right Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the right leg, hold the left foot behind you at the glute with the left hand. Squat down on the right leg until the left knee taps the floor, then drive back to standing. Advanced unilateral squat — heavy right quad and glute load.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat — Bodyweight — Left Leg
setupNotes: Right foot rear-elevated on a chair or low bench, left foot 2–3 feet forward. Lower until the left front thigh is parallel to the floor, drive through the left heel to return. Bodyweight only — clean trainer for the left quad and glute.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat — Bodyweight — Right Leg
setupNotes: Left foot rear-elevated on a chair or low bench, right foot 2–3 feet forward. Lower until the right front thigh is parallel to the floor, drive through the right heel to return. Bodyweight only — clean trainer for the right quad and glute.

name: Jump Squat
setupNotes: Feet shoulder-width, squat down, explode upward leaving the ground. Land softly in squat position. Repeat. Quad and glute power.

name: Lateral Squat — Left Leg
setupNotes: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes forward. Shift the weight to the left, bending the left knee into a deep side squat while the right leg stays straight. Push through the left heel to return to centre. Loads the left adductor and glute.

name: Lateral Squat — Right Leg
setupNotes: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes forward. Shift the weight to the right, bending the right knee into a deep side squat while the left leg stays straight. Push through the right heel to return to centre. Loads the right adductor and glute.

name: Sit-to-Stand
setupNotes: Sit on sturdy chair or bench. Stand up without using hands. Sit back down controlled. Functional leg strength for all levels.

name: Single-Leg Sit-to-Stand — Left Leg
setupNotes: Sit on a chair, left foot planted, right leg extended off the floor. Stand up using only the left leg — drive through the heel without rocking. Lower under control back to sitting. Builds left-leg strength with no equipment.

name: Single-Leg Sit-to-Stand — Right Leg
setupNotes: Sit on a chair, right foot planted, left leg extended off the floor. Stand up using only the right leg — drive through the heel without rocking. Lower under control back to sitting. Builds right-leg strength with no equipment.

name: Reverse Lunge — Bodyweight — Left
setupNotes: Standing tall, hands on hips. Step the left foot back into a long lunge, lowering until both knees reach ~90 degrees and the left back knee hovers above the floor. Drive through the right front heel to return to standing. Loads the right front quad and glute.

name: Reverse Lunge — Bodyweight — Right
setupNotes: Standing tall, hands on hips. Step the right foot back into a long lunge, lowering until both knees reach ~90 degrees and the right back knee hovers above the floor. Drive through the left front heel to return to standing. Loads the left front quad and glute.

name: Forward Lunge — Bodyweight — Left Leg
setupNotes: Standing tall, hands on hips or at sides. Step the left foot forward into a long stride and lower until both knees reach ~90 degrees — front knee tracking over the toes. Push through the left heel to return to standing. Loads the left quad and glute.

name: Forward Lunge — Bodyweight — Right Leg
setupNotes: Standing tall, hands on hips or at sides. Step the right foot forward into a long stride and lower until both knees reach ~90 degrees — front knee tracking over the toes. Push through the right heel to return to standing. Loads the right quad and glute.

name: Jumping Lunge
setupNotes: Start in lunge position. Jump explosively, switch legs mid-air, land in opposite lunge. Continuous. Plyometric cardio and leg power.

name: Static Lunge Hold — Left Leg
setupNotes: Split stance with the left foot forward and right foot back, both knees bent to ~90 degrees. Hold the position with the back knee hovering above the floor and torso upright. Isometric quad and glute endurance through the left front leg.

name: Static Lunge Hold — Right Leg
setupNotes: Split stance with the right foot forward and left foot back, both knees bent to ~90 degrees. Hold the position with the back knee hovering above the floor and torso upright. Isometric quad and glute endurance through the right front leg.

name: Curtsy Lunge — Bodyweight — Left Leg
setupNotes: Standing tall. Step the left foot behind and across the right leg, lowering until the right thigh is parallel to the floor. Drive through the right heel to return to standing. Targets the glute medius.

name: Curtsy Lunge — Bodyweight — Right Leg
setupNotes: Standing tall. Step the right foot behind and across the left leg, lowering until the left thigh is parallel to the floor. Drive through the left heel to return to standing. Targets the glute medius.

name: Glute Bridge
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent, feet flat on floor hip-width. Drive hips up squeezing glutes at top. Lower controlled. Floor exercise.

name: Glute Bridge — Single-Leg — Left Leg
setupNotes: Lie face up, left foot planted hip-width, right knee raised or right leg extended toward the ceiling. Drive the hips up through the left heel until the body is in a straight line, squeeze the left glute hard at the top. Lower under control.

name: Glute Bridge — Single-Leg — Right Leg
setupNotes: Lie face up, right foot planted hip-width, left knee raised or left leg extended toward the ceiling. Drive the hips up through the right heel until the body is in a straight line, squeeze the right glute hard at the top. Lower under control.

name: Glute Bridge — Elevated
setupNotes: Same as standard bridge but feet placed on sturdy chair, bench, or step. Increases range of motion and difficulty.

name: Frog Pump
setupNotes: Lie face up, soles of feet together, knees out to sides (frog position). Drive hips up squeezing glutes. Minimises hamstring involvement.

name: Donkey Kick — Left
setupNotes: On hands and knees in quadruped, mat under knees. Drive left heel toward the ceiling with knee bent 90 degrees, squeezing the glute at top. Controlled return — isolates the left glute.

name: Donkey Kick — Right
setupNotes: On hands and knees in quadruped, mat under knees. Drive right heel toward the ceiling with knee bent 90 degrees, squeezing the glute at top. Controlled return — isolates the right glute.

name: Fire Hydrant — Left
setupNotes: Hands and knees position, spine neutral. Lift the left knee out to the side keeping the 90-degree bend, squeezing the glute at top. Controlled lower — targets the left glute medius.

name: Fire Hydrant — Right
setupNotes: Hands and knees position, spine neutral. Lift the right knee out to the side keeping the 90-degree bend, squeezing the glute at top. Controlled lower — targets the right glute medius.

name: Lateral Band Walk
setupNotes: Mini resistance band around ankles or just above knees. Quarter squat athletic stance. Step sideways maintaining band tension. Continuous side steps.

name: Standing Calf Raise — Bodyweight
setupNotes: Standing on edge of step or flat floor. Rise up onto toes, squeezing calves at top. Controlled lower. Use wall for balance if needed.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — Left Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the left foot at the edge of a step, ball of the foot on the edge and heel hanging off. Hand on a wall for balance. Rise onto the toes as high as possible, then lower the heel below the step for a full stretch. Trains the left calf through full range.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — Right Leg
setupNotes: Standing on the right foot at the edge of a step, ball of the foot on the edge and heel hanging off. Hand on a wall for balance. Rise onto the toes as high as possible, then lower the heel below the step for a full stretch. Trains the right calf through full range.

name: Bodyweight Step-Up
setupNotes: Sturdy chair, bench, or staircase step. Place one foot fully on surface. Drive through heel to stand on top. Step down controlled.

name: March in Place — Standard
setupNotes: Standing, alternate lifting knees to hip height. Pump arms naturally opposite to legs. Controlled pace for warm-up or light cardio.

name: Forearm Plank
setupNotes: Elbows on floor under shoulders, forearms flat. Body straight from head to heels. Engage entire core, breathe steadily. Timed hold.

name: High Plank
setupNotes: Hands under shoulders, arms straight. Body straight, push floor away. Engage core, avoid sagging hips. Foundation position for many exercises.

name: Side Plank — Left Side
setupNotes: Lie on the left side, left forearm on the floor under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered. Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line from head to heels, right arm extended toward the ceiling or on the hip. Hold for time. Loads the left obliques and QL.

name: Side Plank — Right Side
setupNotes: Lie on the right side, right forearm on the floor under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered. Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line from head to heels, left arm extended toward the ceiling or on the hip. Hold for time. Loads the right obliques and QL.

name: Side Plank with Hip Dips — Left Side
setupNotes: Side plank on the left forearm, hips lifted in a straight line. Slowly lower the left hip toward the floor without touching, then drive back up to the start. Controlled reps through full range. Dynamic loading of the left obliques.

name: Side Plank with Hip Dips — Right Side
setupNotes: Side plank on the right forearm, hips lifted in a straight line. Slowly lower the right hip toward the floor without touching, then drive back up to the start. Controlled reps through full range. Dynamic loading of the right obliques.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift — Left Side
setupNotes: Side plank on the left forearm with hips lifted. Raise the right (top) leg upward and hold or pulse at the top while keeping the hips square. Adds glute medius and outer-hip work to the left-side oblique hold.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift — Right Side
setupNotes: Side plank on the right forearm with hips lifted. Raise the left (top) leg upward and hold or pulse at the top while keeping the hips square. Adds glute medius and outer-hip work to the right-side oblique hold.

name: High Plank Knee Drives
setupNotes: High plank position. Drive one knee toward chest quickly, return, repeat other knee. Mountain-climber style from plank. Controlled.

name: Incline Plank (Hands Elevated)
setupNotes: Hands on bench, box, or chair in plank position. Easier regression of floor plank. Good for beginners building core strength.

name: Dead Bug — Standard
setupNotes: Lie face up, arms straight toward ceiling, knees bent 90 degrees (tabletop). Extend opposite arm/leg toward floor, return, alternate. Press lower back into floor.

name: Dead Bug — Slow Tempo
setupNotes: Same position as standard dead bug. Very slow controlled extension (4-5 seconds out, 4-5 seconds back). Focus on maintaining lower back contact with floor.

name: Dead Bug — Banded
setupNotes: Standard dead bug position. Light resistance band looped around hands and/or feet. Band tension adds core demand through full range.

name: Dead Bug — Weighted
setupNotes: Standard dead bug position holding light dumbbell in hands overhead. Extend limbs with control. Added load on core stabilisers.

name: Bird Dog — Standard — Left
setupNotes: On hands and knees, spine neutral. Extend the left arm forward and the right leg back simultaneously until both are parallel to the floor. Brace the core, hold briefly, return. Trains anti-extension and balance.

name: Bird Dog — Standard — Right
setupNotes: On hands and knees, spine neutral. Extend the right arm forward and the left leg back simultaneously until both are parallel to the floor. Brace the core, hold briefly, return. Trains anti-extension and balance.

name: Bird Dog — From Push-Up Position — Left
setupNotes: High plank position, hands under shoulders, body in a straight line. Extend the left arm forward and the right leg back simultaneously, hold briefly without letting the hips rotate. Return. Much harder than the kneeling version.

name: Bird Dog — From Push-Up Position — Right
setupNotes: High plank position, hands under shoulders, body in a straight line. Extend the right arm forward and the left leg back simultaneously, hold briefly without letting the hips rotate. Return. Much harder than the kneeling version.

name: Bird Dog — Band-Resisted — Left
setupNotes: Kneeling bird-dog stance with a light resistance band running from the left hand to the right foot. Extend the left arm and right leg until the band is taut, hold, return. Band adds resistance and instability to the diagonal pattern.

name: Bird Dog — Band-Resisted — Right
setupNotes: Kneeling bird-dog stance with a light resistance band running from the right hand to the left foot. Extend the right arm and left leg until the band is taut, hold, return. Band adds resistance and instability to the diagonal pattern.

name: Bird Dog Row (Weighted) — Left Arm
setupNotes: Kneeling bird-dog stance with a dumbbell in the left hand. Extend the right leg back, then row the left dumbbell to the hip — keeping the hips square and core braced. Lower the dumbbell, return. Combines anti-rotation with a unilateral row.

name: Bird Dog Row (Weighted) — Right Arm
setupNotes: Kneeling bird-dog stance with a dumbbell in the right hand. Extend the left leg back, then row the right dumbbell to the hip — keeping the hips square and core braced. Lower the dumbbell, return. Combines anti-rotation with a unilateral row.

name: Bicycle Crunch — Standard
setupNotes: Lie face up, hands behind head (don't pull neck). Lift shoulders, twist right elbow to left knee while extending right leg. Alternate continuously.

name: Bicycle Crunch — Slow Tempo
setupNotes: Lie face up, hands behind head, shoulders lifted. Slowly twist one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg — 3–4 seconds per side. Full rotation through the torso — maximises oblique time under tension.

name: Standing Bicycle Crunch
setupNotes: Standing, hands behind head. Drive one knee up while rotating opposite elbow to meet it. Alternate sides. Low-impact core work.

name: Lying Leg Raise — Standard
setupNotes: Lie face up, hands under lower back or at sides. Legs straight, lift from floor to vertical. Lower controlled without arching back.

name: Lying Leg Raise — Alternating
setupNotes: Same position as standard. Lift one leg at a time, alternating. Easier progression. Keep lower back pressed into floor.

name: Lying Leg Raise with Hold
setupNotes: Raise both legs to ~6 inches off floor. Hold for prescribed time. Lower back pressed into floor. Isometric lower ab hold.

name: Flutter Kicks
setupNotes: Lie face up, legs extended ~6 inches off floor. Alternate small up/down kicks rapidly. Lower back pressed into floor. Core endurance.

name: Supine Heel Slide — Left
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent, feet flat and pelvis in neutral. Slowly slide the left heel along the floor until the leg is straight, then draw it back under control. Maintain a stable pelvis throughout — trains deep core and lumbopelvic control.

name: Supine Heel Slide — Right
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent, feet flat and pelvis in neutral. Slowly slide the right heel along the floor until the leg is straight, then draw it back under control. Maintain a stable pelvis throughout — trains deep core and lumbopelvic control.

name: Heel Slide with Core Bracing
setupNotes: Same as standard heel slide. Actively brace core (draw navel in) before each slide. Focus on preventing any pelvic movement.

name: Standing Core Brace
setupNotes: Standing, feet hip-width. Draw navel in, engage entire core as if bracing for a punch. Hold for prescribed time while breathing. Foundation drill.

name: Anti-Rotation Brace (Band) — Left
setupNotes: Anchor a light resistance band at chest height to the right side. Stand with the right side toward the anchor, both hands holding the band at the chest. Press the arms straight out and hold — resist the band pulling you into rotation toward the right. Anti-rotation core hold.

name: Anti-Rotation Brace (Band) — Right
setupNotes: Anchor a light resistance band at chest height to the left side. Stand with the left side toward the anchor, both hands holding the band at the chest. Press the arms straight out and hold — resist the band pulling you into rotation toward the left. Anti-rotation core hold.

name: V-Up
setupNotes: Lie face up, arms overhead, legs straight. Simultaneously lift arms and legs to touch hands to feet at top. V shape at peak. Controlled lower.

name: Mountain Climber — Standard
setupNotes: High plank position. Drive one knee toward chest quickly, switch, repeat. Fast alternating like running in place horizontally.

name: Mountain Climber — Cross-Body
setupNotes: High plank position. Drive knee toward opposite elbow. Alternate sides. Rotational element adds oblique engagement to standard climber.

name: High Knees
setupNotes: Standing, drive knees above hip height rapidly alternating legs. Pump arms. Fast pace. On the spot or moving slightly forward.

name: Butt Kicks
setupNotes: Standing, jog in place kicking heels up to touch glutes. Pump arms naturally. Light bounce on balls of feet. Hamstring warm-up and cardio.

name: High Knees + Lateral Shuffle
setupNotes: Combine high knees with lateral shuffling steps. High knees for 4 steps, shuffle 4 steps sideways, repeat. Agility and cardio.

name: High Knee Tuck Jumps
setupNotes: Standing, jump explosively pulling both knees to chest at peak. Land softly with bent knees. Advanced plyometric.

name: Star Jumps
setupNotes: Standing, quarter squat then explode upward spreading arms and legs into X/star shape in air. Land softly in squat. Plyometric full body.

name: Jumping Jacks
setupNotes: Standing, feet together, arms at sides. Jump feet apart while raising arms overhead, jump back. Classic cardio warm-up. Continuous rhythm.

name: Squat Jacks
setupNotes: Like jumping jacks but lower — jump feet wide into squat, then jump feet together to standing. Arms punch out or overhead at top.

name: Box Jump Squat
setupNotes: Stand facing sturdy plyo box or platform. Squat, swing arms, jump onto box landing softly in squat. Step down. Adjust box height to ability.

name: Mountain Climbers — Fast
setupNotes: High plank position. Sprint knees toward chest alternately as fast as possible. Maintain plank integrity. HIIT cardio from plank.

name: Spider Mountain Climbers
setupNotes: High plank. Bring knee to outside of same-side elbow (wider than standard climber). Alternate. Hip mobility plus core work.

name: Squat-to-Stand
setupNotes: Standing, fold forward touching toes (bend knees if needed). Grab toes, squat hips down, lift chest to deep squat. Stand up. Repeat. Mobility and legs.

name: Burpee
setupNotes: Standing, squat down placing hands on floor. Jump feet back to plank, perform push-up (optional), jump feet to hands, jump up with arms overhead. Full body.

name: Fast Feet
setupNotes: Athletic stance, slightly bent knees. Rapid small steps in place, feet barely leaving ground. Fast as possible for prescribed time. Agility drill.

name: Battle Ropes — Alternating Waves
setupNotes: Stand with knees slightly bent, one rope end in each hand. Alternate arms creating continuous waves in rope. Full body cardio.

name: Battle Ropes — Power Slam
setupNotes: Stand with knees slightly bent, both rope ends. Raise both arms overhead then slam ropes down together. Squat with slam. Full body power.

name: Battle Ropes — Side-to-Side Slam
setupNotes: Hold both ropes, sweep them side to side together creating lateral waves. Core rotation with upper body power. Oblique emphasis.

name: Battle Ropes — Kneeling Waves
setupNotes: Kneel on mat, one rope end in each hand. Alternating waves from kneeling position. Removes legs, isolates upper body and core.

name: Sled Push — Standard
setupNotes: Load sled with moderate weight. Grip high or low handles. Drive forward with legs, steady pace for distance. Lean into sled.

name: Sled Push — Heavy (Strength)
setupNotes: Load sled heavy. Low handle grip, lean forward at ~45 degrees. Short powerful steps, drive through toes. Strength and leg power focus.

name: Sled Push — Sprint
setupNotes: Light-moderate load on sled. High handles or low. Sprint for short distance (20-40 metres). Maximum speed effort.

name: Sled Push — Reverse (Backward)
setupNotes: Face sled, grip handles, walk or drive backward pulling sled toward you with each step. Quad-dominant movement. Knee-friendly.

name: Sled Pull — Hand-Over-Hand
setupNotes: Attach long rope to sled. Sit or stand at end of rope. Pull sled toward you hand over hand. Upper back and bicep emphasis.

name: Sled Pull — Backward Walk
setupNotes: Attach strap to sled, harness around waist. Walk backward pulling sled. Upright torso. Quad and glute emphasis.

name: Skipping Rope
setupNotes: Jump rope on firm flat surface. Light bounce on balls of feet, wrists control rope rotation. Various speeds and footwork patterns.

name: Bear Crawl
setupNotes: On hands and feet (not knees), knees hovering just off ground. Crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together. Core and full body.

name: Treadmill Walk
setupNotes: Treadmill set to comfortable walking speed (4-6 km/h). Upright posture, arms swinging naturally. Incline optional for added effort.

name: Treadmill Jog
setupNotes: Treadmill set to jogging pace (7-9 km/h). Easy conversational pace. Land mid-foot, relaxed shoulders and arms.

name: Treadmill Run
setupNotes: Treadmill set to running pace (10-14 km/h). Moderate to hard effort. Good running form — upright posture, mid-foot strike, relaxed hands.

name: Treadmill Sprint
setupNotes: Treadmill set to sprint speed (15+ km/h) or maximum effort for short intervals (15-30 seconds). Hold side rails to mount/dismount safely.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
setupNotes: Treadmill at walking speed with incline raised (8-15%). Walk uphill. Do not hold handrails for full benefit. Glute and cardio emphasis.

name: Stationary Bike — Steady
setupNotes: Adjust seat height so slight bend at bottom of pedal stroke. Steady moderate resistance. Upright or recumbent position. Sustained pace.

name: Spin Bike — Standing Climb
setupNotes: Spin bike with heavy resistance. Stand on pedals and pedal while standing, simulating uphill climb. Grip handlebars firmly.

name: Rower — Steady
setupNotes: Rowing machine. Strap feet in, grip handle. Drive with legs first, then lean back, then pull arms. Reverse sequence on return. Steady pace.

name: Rower — Sprint Intervals
setupNotes: Rowing machine. Alternate between max-effort sprints (20-30 seconds) and easy recovery rowing (60-90 seconds). Damper setting at 4-6.

name: Elliptical — Steady
setupNotes: Elliptical machine. Feet on pedals, grip moving or stationary handles. Smooth pedalling motion. Moderate resistance, steady pace.

name: Elliptical — Intervals
setupNotes: Elliptical machine. Alternate between high resistance/speed bursts and easy recovery. Use both handles for upper and lower body.

name: Elliptical — Reverse Pedal
setupNotes: Elliptical machine, pedal in reverse direction. Quad emphasis changes compared to forward motion. Grip handles for stability.

name: StairMaster — Steady Climb
setupNotes: StairMaster or stepmill. Steady stepping pace, hands light on rails (don't lean on them). Upright posture. Glute and cardio focus.

name: StairMaster — Intervals
setupNotes: StairMaster. Alternate fast and slow stepping, or change levels. Hands off rails for best effect. Short burst high effort, longer recovery.

name: Assault / Air Bike — Intervals
setupNotes: Air bike / assault bike. Arms and legs drive together. Sprint intervals (20-30 sec on, 60-90 sec off). Total body cardio.

name: Ski Erg
setupNotes: Ski erg machine. Stand, grip handles overhead. Pull down using lats and core, hinge slightly at hips. Return arms overhead. Steady or interval pace.

name: High Knee March
setupNotes: Standing, drive knees above hip level alternately. Pump arms opposite to legs. Moderate pace. Hip flexor activation and warm-up.

name: Arm Swings — Forward
setupNotes: Standing, swing both arms forward and up overhead in large arcs — then back down. Build momentum with each rep. Dynamic shoulder warm-up.

name: Arm Swings — Backward
setupNotes: Standing, swing both arms backward in large reverse arcs — pulling shoulders back and opening chest. Build momentum with each rep. Dynamic shoulder warm-up.

name: Cross-Body Arm Swings
setupNotes: Standing, swing both arms horizontally across body in alternating cross pattern. Opens chest and warms up shoulders and pecs.

name: Hip Circles
setupNotes: Stand with feet hip-width apart, hands on hips. Rotate hips in large smooth circles — clockwise then counterclockwise. Keep upper body stable. Warms up hip joints and lower back.

name: Ankle Circles
setupNotes: Standing on one leg (hold support), rotate foot in circles. Clockwise then counterclockwise. 10 each direction. Switch feet.

name: Wrist Rolls
setupNotes: Extend arms forward, circle wrists in both directions. Open and close fists between circles. Warms up wrist joints for pressing and gripping.

name: Leg Swings — Front to Back (Left Leg)
setupNotes: Stand with the right side near a wall, right hand on the wall for balance. Swing the left leg forward and backward in a controlled pendulum, gradually increasing range. Warms up the left hip flexors and hamstrings.
parentName: Leg Swings — Front to Back (Left Leg)

name: Leg Swings — Front to Back (Right Leg)
setupNotes: Stand with the left side near a wall, left hand on the wall for balance. Swing the right leg forward and backward in a controlled pendulum, gradually increasing range. Warms up the right hip flexors and hamstrings.
parentName: Leg Swings — Front to Back (Right Leg)

name: Leg Swings — Side to Side (Left Leg)
setupNotes: Face a wall, both hands on it for support, weight on the right leg. Swing the left leg across the body and out to the side in a controlled pendulum. Warms up the left adductors and abductors.
parentName: Leg Swings — Side to Side (Left Leg)

name: Leg Swings — Side to Side (Right Leg)
setupNotes: Face a wall, both hands on it for support, weight on the left leg. Swing the right leg across the body and out to the side in a controlled pendulum. Warms up the right adductors and abductors.
parentName: Leg Swings — Side to Side (Right Leg)

name: Cat-Cow
setupNotes: On hands and knees. Alternate between arching back (cow — belly drops) and rounding back (cat — belly lifts). Coordinate with breathing.

name: Inchworm
setupNotes: Standing, fold forward touching floor. Walk hands out to plank position. Optional push-up. Walk feet to hands, stand up. Full body warm-up.

name: Walking Lunge with Twist
setupNotes: Step into forward lunge, rotate torso toward front leg. Arms extended or hands together. Return to standing, step other leg. Dynamic stretch.

name: Scapular Push-Up
setupNotes: High plank position, arms straight. Without bending elbows, push shoulder blades apart (protract) then squeeze together (retract). Scapular mobility.

name: Shoulder Rolls
setupNotes: Standing, roll shoulders forward in circles, then backward. Big controlled circles. Loosens upper traps and shoulder joints.

name: Child's Pose
setupNotes: Kneel on mat, sit back on heels, extend arms forward on floor. Forehead rests on ground. Deep breathing. Stretches back, lats, and hips.

name: Seated Forward Fold
setupNotes: Sit on floor, legs extended straight. Hinge forward at hips reaching toward feet. Hold. Stretches hamstrings and lower back.

name: Standing Quad Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Standing tall, free hand on a wall for balance. Pull the left foot up toward the left glute with the left hand, knees together and hips pressed forward slightly. Hold and breathe. Stretches the left quad and hip flexor.

name: Standing Quad Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Standing tall, free hand on a wall for balance. Pull the right foot up toward the right glute with the right hand, knees together and hips pressed forward slightly. Hold and breathe. Stretches the right quad and hip flexor.

name: Hamstring Stretch — Seated — Left
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with the left leg extended and the right foot tucked against the inner left thigh. Hinge at the hips and reach over the left leg, back flat. Hold and breathe. Targets the left hamstring.

name: Hamstring Stretch — Seated — Right
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with the right leg extended and the left foot tucked against the inner right thigh. Hinge at the hips and reach over the right leg, back flat. Hold and breathe. Targets the right hamstring.

name: Hamstring Stretch — Standing — Left
setupNotes: Standing, place the left heel on a low bench or step with the leg straight. Hinge from the hips and lean forward over the left leg, keeping the back flat. Hold. Targets the left hamstring.

name: Hamstring Stretch — Standing — Right
setupNotes: Standing, place the right heel on a low bench or step with the leg straight. Hinge from the hips and lean forward over the right leg, keeping the back flat. Hold. Targets the right hamstring.

name: Calf Stretch — Wall (Left Leg)
setupNotes: Face a wall in a split stance — left foot back with the heel pressed to the floor, right foot forward with the knee bent. Lean the hips toward the wall until the left calf stretches. Hold. Targets the left gastrocnemius.

name: Calf Stretch — Wall (Right Leg)
setupNotes: Face a wall in a split stance — right foot back with the heel pressed to the floor, left foot forward with the knee bent. Lean the hips toward the wall until the right calf stretches. Hold. Targets the right gastrocnemius.

name: Chest Stretch — Doorway — Left
setupNotes: Stand in a doorway, left forearm against the frame with the elbow at 90 degrees and shoulder height. Step the left foot through the doorway and rotate the chest away from the arm until a stretch is felt across the left pec and front shoulder. Hold.

name: Chest Stretch — Doorway — Right
setupNotes: Stand in a doorway, right forearm against the frame with the elbow at 90 degrees and shoulder height. Step the right foot through the doorway and rotate the chest away from the arm until a stretch is felt across the right pec and front shoulder. Hold.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Standing tall, bring the left arm straight across the chest. Hook the right forearm under the left elbow and pull the left arm closer to the body. Hold. Stretches the left rear delt and upper back.

name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Standing tall, bring the right arm straight across the chest. Hook the left forearm under the right elbow and pull the right arm closer to the body. Hold. Stretches the right rear delt and upper back.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Raise the left arm overhead and bend the elbow so the left hand drops behind the head. Use the right hand to gently press the left elbow back and down. Hold. Stretches the left triceps and lat.

name: Overhead Triceps Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Raise the right arm overhead and bend the elbow so the right hand drops behind the head. Use the left hand to gently press the right elbow back and down. Hold. Stretches the right triceps and lat.

name: Hip Flexor Stretch — Left Hip
setupNotes: Half-kneeling on the mat — left knee down, right foot forward. Tuck the pelvis under and gently push the hips forward until a stretch is felt at the front of the left hip. Stay tall through the torso. Hold. Stretches the left hip flexor.

name: Hip Flexor Stretch — Right Hip
setupNotes: Half-kneeling on the mat — right knee down, left foot forward. Tuck the pelvis under and gently push the hips forward until a stretch is felt at the front of the right hip. Stay tall through the torso. Hold. Stretches the right hip flexor.

name: Glute Stretch — Figure 4 — Left
setupNotes: Lie face up with knees bent. Cross the left ankle over the right knee in a figure-4. Reach through and pull the right thigh toward the chest until a stretch is felt deep in the left glute. Hold. Targets the left piriformis.

name: Glute Stretch — Figure 4 — Right
setupNotes: Lie face up with knees bent. Cross the right ankle over the left knee in a figure-4. Reach through and pull the left thigh toward the chest until a stretch is felt deep in the right glute. Hold. Targets the right piriformis.

name: Neck Side Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Standing or seated tall, gently tilt the right ear toward the right shoulder, keeping the left shoulder relaxed and pressed down. Optionally use the right hand for light additional pressure. Hold. Stretches the left side of the neck.

name: Neck Side Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Standing or seated tall, gently tilt the left ear toward the left shoulder, keeping the right shoulder relaxed and pressed down. Optionally use the left hand for light additional pressure. Hold. Stretches the right side of the neck.

name: Upper Trap Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Seated tall, place the left hand behind the back. Tilt the head away from the left shoulder and use the right hand on the head for gentle additional pressure. Hold. Releases tension in the left upper trap.

name: Upper Trap Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Seated tall, place the right hand behind the back. Tilt the head away from the right shoulder and use the left hand on the head for gentle additional pressure. Hold. Releases tension in the right upper trap.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing — Supine
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent, feet flat. One hand on chest, one on belly. Breathe deeply into belly (belly rises), chest stays still. Slow exhale.

name: Diaphragmatic Breathing — Seated
setupNotes: Sit upright in chair, feet flat. Hands on belly. Inhale through nose expanding belly. Exhale slowly through mouth. Relaxed shoulders.

name: Pelvic-Balloon Breathing
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent. Visualise pelvic floor as balloon inflating on inhale (relaxes down) and deflating on exhale (draws up). Coordinate breath.

name: Kegel — Slow Hold
setupNotes: Seated or supine. Contract pelvic floor muscles (as if stopping urine flow). Hold for 5-10 seconds, fully relax for same duration. Repeat.

name: Kegel — Quick Flicks
setupNotes: Same position. Rapidly contract and release pelvic floor muscles. 1-second hold, 1-second release. Builds fast-twitch pelvic floor response.

name: Kegel — Endurance Set
setupNotes: Seated or supine. Contract pelvic floor and hold for increasing durations (10, 15, 20 seconds). Full relaxation between holds.

name: Pelvic Tilts
setupNotes: Lie face up, knees bent, feet flat. Gently tilt pelvis — flatten lower back against floor (posterior tilt), then release to neutral. Gentle rocking motion.

name: Clamshell — Standard — Left
setupNotes: Lie on the right side, knees bent to 90 degrees, feet stacked together. Keep the feet touching and open the left (top) knee upward like a clamshell, squeezing the left glute medius. Lower under control.

name: Clamshell — Standard — Right
setupNotes: Lie on the left side, knees bent to 90 degrees, feet stacked together. Keep the feet touching and open the right (top) knee upward like a clamshell, squeezing the right glute medius. Lower under control.

name: Clamshell — Banded — Left
setupNotes: Lie on the right side with a mini band looped just above the knees, knees bent to 90 degrees and feet stacked. Open the left (top) knee against the band's resistance, squeezing the left glute medius. Lower under control.

name: Clamshell — Banded — Right
setupNotes: Lie on the left side with a mini band looped just above the knees, knees bent to 90 degrees and feet stacked. Open the right (top) knee against the band's resistance, squeezing the right glute medius. Lower under control.

name: Reverse Clamshell — Left
setupNotes: Lie on the right side, knees bent and stacked. Keep the knees pressed together and lift the left (top) foot upward, rotating from the left hip. Lower under control. Trains internal rotation of the left hip.

name: Reverse Clamshell — Right
setupNotes: Lie on the left side, knees bent and stacked. Keep the knees pressed together and lift the right (top) foot upward, rotating from the right hip. Lower under control. Trains internal rotation of the right hip.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch — Left Hip
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with the left leg in front bent to 90 degrees (shin across the body) and the right leg bent 90 degrees out to the side behind. Square the hips and lean the torso forward over the left shin. Hold. Opens the left external rotators.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch — Right Hip
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with the right leg in front bent to 90 degrees (shin across the body) and the left leg bent 90 degrees out to the side behind. Square the hips and lean the torso forward over the right shin. Hold. Opens the right external rotators.

name: Scapular Squeeze — Standing
setupNotes: Standing, arms at sides or slightly raised. Squeeze shoulder blades together and down. Hold 5 seconds, release. Posture and upper back activation.

name: Resistance Band Scapular Retraction
setupNotes: Anchor band at chest height. Hold with straight arms. Pull shoulder blades together without bending elbows. Release controlled.

name: Band Pull-Apart
setupNotes: Hold resistance band at chest height with straight arms, shoulder-width grip. Pull band apart by squeezing shoulder blades together. Controlled return.

name: Band Pull-Apart — 3 Position
setupNotes: Perform band pull-aparts at three heights: overhead, eye level, and chest level. Hits rear delts and rhomboids from different angles.

name: Band Y-Raise
setupNotes: Stand on or anchor band low. Arms straight, raise into Y-shape overhead (arms at ~45 degrees from body). Lower controlled. Lower trap activation.

name: Band T-Raise
setupNotes: Stand on or anchor band low. Arms straight, raise to sides forming a T (arms horizontal). Lower controlled. Middle trap and rear delt.

name: Band W-Raise
setupNotes: Stand on or anchor band low. Pull into W-shape — elbows bent, upper arms at 45 degrees, hands at ear level. Squeeze shoulder blades. Rotator cuff.

name: External Rotation — Band (Left Arm)
setupNotes: Anchor a band at elbow height to the right. Stand with the right side toward the anchor, hold the band in the left hand with the elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the forearm outward away from the body against the band. Trains the left rotator cuff (infraspinatus/teres minor).

name: External Rotation — Band (Right Arm)
setupNotes: Anchor a band at elbow height to the left. Stand with the left side toward the anchor, hold the band in the right hand with the elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the forearm outward away from the body against the band. Trains the right rotator cuff (infraspinatus/teres minor).

name: External Rotation — 90 Degree
setupNotes: Anchor band at shoulder height. Elbow at 90 degrees at shoulder height. Rotate forearm from pointing down to pointing up against band. Cuff rehab.

name: Internal Rotation — Band (Left Arm)
setupNotes: Anchor a band at elbow height to the left. Stand with the left side toward the anchor, hold the band in the left hand with the elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the forearm inward across the body against the band. Trains the left subscapularis.

name: Internal Rotation — Band (Right Arm)
setupNotes: Anchor a band at elbow height to the right. Stand with the right side toward the anchor, hold the band in the right hand with the elbow pinned to the side and bent to 90 degrees. Rotate the forearm inward across the body against the band. Trains the right subscapularis.

name: Overhead Arm Hold
setupNotes: Standing, hold light dumbbells or no weight with arms straight overhead. Hold for time. Shoulder endurance and thoracic mobility.

name: T-Hold (Lateral Arm Hold)
setupNotes: Standing, arms extended straight to sides at shoulder height. Hold for prescribed time. Shoulder endurance, medial deltoid isometric.

name: Single-Leg Balance Hold — Left Leg
setupNotes: Stand on the left foot, right foot lifted just off the floor. Hold for 30–60 seconds, eyes forward. Close the eyes for additional challenge. Trains left ankle stability and proprioception.

name: Single-Leg Balance Hold — Right Leg
setupNotes: Stand on the right foot, left foot lifted just off the floor. Hold for 30–60 seconds, eyes forward. Close the eyes for additional challenge. Trains right ankle stability and proprioception.

name: Dead Bug with Physio Ball
setupNotes: Lie face up, squeeze physio ball between hands and knees. Extend opposite arm and leg while maintaining ball pressure with other limbs.

name: Swiss Ball V-Pass
setupNotes: Lie face up, swiss ball in hands overhead. Crunch up passing ball from hands to feet, lower. Next rep pass back to hands.

name: Stability Ball Leg Extension Dead Bug
setupNotes: Lie face up, calves on stability ball. Dead bug arm movements while legs maintain contact with ball. Core stability focus.

name: BOSU Ball Dead Bug
setupNotes: Lie face up on BOSU ball (dome up) for added instability. Perform dead bug arm/leg extensions. BOSU challenges balance and core control.

name: Superman with Physio Ball + Shoulder ROM
setupNotes: Lie prone, hold physio ball in both hands. Lift chest and ball, then move ball through full shoulder range of motion overhead.

name: Swiss Ball V-Pass Dead Bug
setupNotes: Lie face up, swiss ball held overhead. Pass ball between hands and feet while maintaining dead bug core engagement pattern.

name: Stability Ball Jackknife
setupNotes: High plank position with shins on stability ball. Pull knees toward chest rolling ball forward (jackknife). Extend back to plank.

name: Swiss Ball Side Plank with Leg Lift
setupNotes: Side plank position with feet on swiss ball. Lift top leg while holding side plank. Ball adds instability. Core and hip work.

name: Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl
setupNotes: Lie face up, heels on top of swiss ball, hips lifted. Curl ball toward glutes by bending knees, extend back. Hips stay elevated.

name: Swiss Ball Hip Flexor Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Kneeling lunge with the left shin resting on a swiss ball behind, right foot forward. Tuck the pelvis under and push the hips forward until a stretch is felt at the front of the left hip. Ball cushions the shin and adds slight instability.

name: Swiss Ball Hip Flexor Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Kneeling lunge with the right shin resting on a swiss ball behind, left foot forward. Tuck the pelvis under and push the hips forward until a stretch is felt at the front of the right hip. Ball cushions the shin and adds slight instability.

name: Foam Roll — Upper Back
setupNotes: Foam roller on floor. Lie on roller positioned under upper back. Arms crossed on chest. Roll from mid-back to upper traps. Pause on tight spots.

name: Foam Roll — Lats — Left
setupNotes: Lie on the left side with a foam roller under the left armpit/lat area, left arm extended overhead. Roll slowly from the armpit down to the mid-ribcage, pausing on tender spots. Releases the left lat.

name: Foam Roll — Lats — Right
setupNotes: Lie on the right side with a foam roller under the right armpit/lat area, right arm extended overhead. Roll slowly from the armpit down to the mid-ribcage, pausing on tender spots. Releases the right lat.

name: Foam Roll — Quads
setupNotes: Lie face down, foam roller under front of thighs. Roll from just above knee to hip flexor. Support weight with forearms. Pause on tight spots.

name: Foam Roll — IT Band — Left
setupNotes: Lie on the left side with a foam roller under the left outer thigh, right leg crossed over for support. Roll slowly from just above the knee up to the hip. Releases the left IT band — slow and tolerable.

name: Foam Roll — IT Band — Right
setupNotes: Lie on the right side with a foam roller under the right outer thigh, left leg crossed over for support. Roll slowly from just above the knee up to the hip. Releases the right IT band — slow and tolerable.

name: Foam Roll — Hamstrings
setupNotes: Sit on floor, foam roller under back of thighs. Roll from just above knee to sit bones. Hands behind for support. Cross legs for more pressure.

name: Foam Roll — Calves — Left
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under the left calf, right leg crossed over the left for added pressure. Hands behind for support, lift the hips and roll from the Achilles up to just below the knee. Rotate the leg to hit medial and lateral fibres.

name: Foam Roll — Calves — Right
setupNotes: Sit on the floor with a foam roller under the right calf, left leg crossed over the right for added pressure. Hands behind for support, lift the hips and roll from the Achilles up to just below the knee. Rotate the leg to hit medial and lateral fibres.

name: Foam Roll — Glutes — Left
setupNotes: Sit on a foam roller, cross the left ankle over the right knee in a figure-4. Lean the weight toward the left side and roll slowly over the left glute, pausing on tender spots. Targeted release of the left glute and piriformis.

name: Foam Roll — Glutes — Right
setupNotes: Sit on a foam roller, cross the right ankle over the left knee in a figure-4. Lean the weight toward the right side and roll slowly over the right glute, pausing on tender spots. Targeted release of the right glute and piriformis.

name: Lacrosse Ball — Piriformis — Left
setupNotes: Sit on a lacrosse ball positioned under the left glute/piriformis, left ankle crossed over the right knee in a figure-4. Roll gently or hold pressure on the tender spot. Releases the left piriformis.

name: Lacrosse Ball — Piriformis — Right
setupNotes: Sit on a lacrosse ball positioned under the right glute/piriformis, right ankle crossed over the left knee in a figure-4. Roll gently or hold pressure on the tender spot. Releases the right piriformis.

name: Lacrosse Ball — Shoulder/Rear Delt — Left
setupNotes: Stand with a lacrosse ball pinned between the left upper back/rear delt and a wall. Lean into the ball to apply pressure and roll in small circles to find tight spots. Releases the left rear delt and upper trap.

name: Lacrosse Ball — Shoulder/Rear Delt — Right
setupNotes: Stand with a lacrosse ball pinned between the right upper back/rear delt and a wall. Lean into the ball to apply pressure and roll in small circles to find tight spots. Releases the right rear delt and upper trap.

name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
setupNotes: Sit on floor with front leg bent 90 degrees in front and back leg bent 90 degrees to the side. Lean forward over the front shin to deepen the stretch through the front hip. Hip opener — switch sides to work both hips.

name: World's Greatest Stretch — Left
setupNotes: From standing, step the left foot forward into a deep lunge and place both hands on the floor inside the left foot. Rotate the torso toward the left knee and reach the left arm up toward the ceiling. Hold, then return. Mobilises the left hip, T-spine, and hamstring.

name: World's Greatest Stretch — Right
setupNotes: From standing, step the right foot forward into a deep lunge and place both hands on the floor inside the right foot. Rotate the torso toward the right knee and reach the right arm up toward the ceiling. Hold, then return. Mobilises the right hip, T-spine, and hamstring.

name: Pigeon Stretch — Left
setupNotes: From hands and knees, slide the left knee forward behind the left wrist with the shin angled across the body. Extend the right leg straight back. Lower the torso over the left shin. Hold and breathe. Deep stretch of the left external rotators and glute.

name: Pigeon Stretch — Right
setupNotes: From hands and knees, slide the right knee forward behind the right wrist with the shin angled across the body. Extend the left leg straight back. Lower the torso over the right shin. Hold and breathe. Deep stretch of the right external rotators and glute.

name: Thread the Needle — Left
setupNotes: On hands and knees, reach the left arm under the body through the space between the right hand and right knee, lowering the left shoulder and ear to the floor. Hold and breathe. Rotates the left thoracic spine.

name: Thread the Needle — Right
setupNotes: On hands and knees, reach the right arm under the body through the space between the left hand and left knee, lowering the right shoulder and ear to the floor. Hold and breathe. Rotates the right thoracic spine.

name: Couch Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Kneel facing away from a wall with the left shin pressed up against it (toes pointing up), right foot forward in a lunge. Tuck the pelvis and push the hips forward, staying tall. Intense stretch of the left quad and hip flexor.

name: Couch Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Kneel facing away from a wall with the right shin pressed up against it (toes pointing up), left foot forward in a lunge. Tuck the pelvis and push the hips forward, staying tall. Intense stretch of the right quad and hip flexor.

name: Banded Shoulder Distraction — Left
setupNotes: Anchor a heavy band to a rack at shoulder height. Loop the band around the left wrist and step away to create tension, then drop into a lunge or hinge so the band gently distracts the left shoulder. Hold and breathe. Mobilises the left shoulder capsule.

name: Banded Shoulder Distraction — Right
setupNotes: Anchor a heavy band to a rack at shoulder height. Loop the band around the right wrist and step away to create tension, then drop into a lunge or hinge so the band gently distracts the right shoulder. Hold and breathe. Mobilises the right shoulder capsule.

name: Wall Thoracic Extension
setupNotes: Stand facing wall, arms overhead on wall. Slowly push chest toward wall, arching upper back. Hold stretch. Thoracic extension mobility.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch — Left
setupNotes: Half-kneeling facing a wall — right knee down, left foot forward 4–6 inches from the wall. Drive the left knee forward toward the wall without lifting the left heel off the floor. Mobilises the left ankle into dorsiflexion.

name: Ankle Dorsiflexion Stretch — Right
setupNotes: Half-kneeling facing a wall — left knee down, right foot forward 4–6 inches from the wall. Drive the right knee forward toward the wall without lifting the right heel off the floor. Mobilises the right ankle into dorsiflexion.

name: Supine Spinal Twist — Left
setupNotes: Lie face up, arms out in a T. Pull the left knee up and across the body to the right side, keeping both shoulders pressed to the floor. Let gravity carry the left knee down. Hold and breathe. Gentle rotation of the lumbar spine.

name: Supine Spinal Twist — Right
setupNotes: Lie face up, arms out in a T. Pull the right knee up and across the body to the left side, keeping both shoulders pressed to the floor. Let gravity carry the right knee down. Hold and breathe. Gentle rotation of the lumbar spine.

name: Supine Hamstring Stretch with Band — Left
setupNotes: Lie face up with a strap or band looped around the left foot. Extend the left leg toward the ceiling, keeping the knee soft, and gently pull the band for a deeper stretch. Right leg stays flat on the floor. Targets the left hamstring.

name: Supine Hamstring Stretch with Band — Right
setupNotes: Lie face up with a strap or band looped around the right foot. Extend the right leg toward the ceiling, keeping the knee soft, and gently pull the band for a deeper stretch. Left leg stays flat on the floor. Targets the right hamstring.

name: L-Sit Pull-Up
setupNotes: Hang from a pull-up bar with shoulder-width overhand grip. Raise legs to a 90-degree L-sit and hold the position throughout. Pull chest to bar keeping legs locked out — lower with control. Advanced — combines isometric core hold with vertical pull.

name: High Side Plank — Left Side
setupNotes: Lie on side with bottom hand on floor directly under shoulder, arm fully straight. Stack or stagger feet. Press the floor away and lift hips into a straight line — top arm extended overhead or on hip. Targets obliques and shoulder stability.

name: High Side Plank — Right Side
setupNotes: Lie on side with bottom hand on floor directly under shoulder, arm fully straight. Stack or stagger feet. Press the floor away and lift hips into a straight line — top arm extended overhead or on hip. Targets obliques and shoulder stability.

name: Arm Swings — Lateral
setupNotes: Standing, swing both arms forward and up overhead in large arcs — then back down. Build momentum with each rep. Dynamic shoulder warm-up.

name: Arm Swings — Forward/Backward Continuous
setupNotes: Standing, swing both arms forward and up overhead in large arcs — then back down. Build momentum with each rep. Dynamic shoulder warm-up.

name: Bird Dog Hold
setupNotes: On hands and knees, spine neutral. Extend the left arm forward and the right leg back simultaneously until both are parallel to the floor. Brace the core, hold briefly, return. Trains anti-extension and balance.

name: Plank to Push-Up
setupNotes: Start in forearm plank. Push up to high plank one arm at a time, then lower back to forearms. Alternate lead arm each rep.
